lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: CHAPTER 32

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Inventory of Ghosts
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The scraping stopped before Zeek could turn.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Whatever the wall had done to his name, it left no mark he could see. The limestone remained smooth where his own account should have been. Only the residual heat under the linen on his palm told him the chisel had finished its first pass.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg was still staring at Ninsun.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Who?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: he asked again.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The silence that followed was not empty. It had weight, the particular density of a room holding its breath to see which of them would be the first to disturb it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg's grip on his axe had gone loose. He regarded Ninsun with the polite, distant curiosity reserved for a stranger bumped into in a crowded market—a flicker of acknowledgment, nothing more, no history behind the eyes at all.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: She's a scholar,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek said. The words tasted like ash.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Ninsun. She's been with us since the gate.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He kept his voice level, the way he might speak to a spooked animal, though he was no longer certain whether the effort was for BAH-lahg's benefit or his own.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg frowned. The information seemed to travel a great distance to reach him, losing pieces of itself along the way.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: No,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: he said slowly.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: We were three. You, me, and the knife-woman.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He gestured vaguely toward en-HEH-doo, who watched without reacting, the figurine turning slowly in her hands.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I don't know who told you to follow us, but you're a liability.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun stepped forward and reached for his arm. He flinched away as though her hand carried contagion.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Don't.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek's mind moved through the cold arithmetic of the situation the way he had once turned over the mechanics of a trap before deciding where to place his foot. If the City had edited BAH-lahg's memory, what exactly had it put in the empty space where Ninsun used to be? A simple blank? Or an alternate history, complete and self-consistent, in which she had never existed and the three of them had always been three?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The second possibility was worse.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun turned to him.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Tell him.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I already did.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Tell him again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek opened his mouth. For a moment the words would not form. The shape of Ninsun's presence was still there—the scholar who had argued for knowledge over silver, who had copied the map until her fingers stained, who had watched his face as if trying to memorize it—but the specific reasons she belonged with them had begun to soften at the edges, the way a word softens in the mouth right before it is lost.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He stared at her face and felt the absence of a reason even while knowing, with a certainty that had nothing to do with evidence, that there had once been one. The way a man missing a tooth can feel the exact size and shape of the gap without being able to describe the tooth itself.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Zeek,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun whispered.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Don't let it count me.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The scratching stopped.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Every sound in the chamber vanished with it, all at once, the way a held breath finally lets go.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg turned slowly. en-HEH-doo looked up from the figurine. Zeek felt something move inside BAH-lahg's pack—not shift, not settle, but move, deliberately, the canvas bulging once before subsiding again into stillness.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He reached for the journal.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The words on the page began to change before his eyes, wet ink spreading and reforming with the slow, deliberate patience of a hand that had all the time in the world:

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: THREE WERE SENT INTO THE CITY.
lines.note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: THREE REMAIN.
lines.note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He looked at the three people standing around him—BAH-lahg, en-HEH-doo, Ninsun—and then, finally, at himself.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Which of us is not one of the three?
lines.note: Internal thought; intimate, not voiced aloud.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Something knocked from inside BAH-lahg's pack.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Once.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Twice.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Three times.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Each strike as precise and unhurried as the last.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg reached slowly for the straps, his face gone slack with a curiosity that had no fear in it yet. Zeek grabbed his wrist before he could open it.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Don't.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked down at the journal as the final line finished writing itself, the ink drawing out each letter with excruciating deliberation:

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: ONE OF YOU WAS NEVER SENT.
lines.note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The chamber seemed to contract around them. The walls leaned inward as if to hear better. Ninsun made a small, strangled sound. en-HEH-doo's earlier detachment cracked into something closer to alarm. BAH-lahg's face had gone the color of old ash.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: From inside the pack came a fourth knock.
